response.consequence: With any missing or duplicated error event, the error context sent to Seer carries wrong event ids. The summary can then mislabel errors.
response.explanation: nodestore.get_multi returns a dict keyed by node id. It deduplicates ids and only includes ids it found, so missing events are absent. The code zips error_ids with events.values(). If any error event is missing from nodestore, or an id is duplicated, every later value is paired with the wrong event_id. The `id` field then belongs to a different event. Because the filter `if data is not None` is applied after the zip, it never catches the missing entries, since missing keys are simply absent. The `id` is also not the node id the dict is keyed by.

other_findings.consequence: Seer receives all errors at the start of the log instead of at their position in the timeline. This degrades summary accuracy. Because error_events are passed to every page, the errors are also repeated in each paginated segment page.
other_findings.explanation: gen_request_data compares error_events[i]["timestamp"], taken from the nodestore event payload, with event.get("timestamp", 0) from the replay recording segments. Nodestore event timestamps are epoch seconds. Replay recording event timestamps are epoch milliseconds. Every error is therefore numerically smaller than every replay event. All errors are emitted before the first replay event, so they are not interleaved chronologically as the docstring promises.
other_findings.title: Error timestamps (seconds) compared against replay event timestamps (milliseconds)
